learning: Iteration 7 lowered yaw inertia and raised slalom progress to 0.53 with line loss at 1.3. Iteration 4 versus 1 showed that narrower track gave a slalom gain with no oval loss. This race tests the next step of that lever.
notes: Runnable package: the Builder's iteration 8 geometry (iteration 7 design with wheel_track 0.09 m) on the iteration 7 controller. Only wheel_track differs from the raced design, so the race isolates turn authority at the slalom.
rationale: Iteration 7 (mass 0.6 kg, body_length 0.12 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, span ±0.036 m, lead 0.06 m, kp 3.6, kd 0.9) is the best design so far at 707.2. Its s-bend finished 20/20 with steering_oscillation 0.311, under the 0.35 limit. Its oval finished 20/20 at 1.79 s. The slalom is still 0/20, with mean progress up from 0.30 to 0.53 and line_loss_events up to 1.3, which means lower yaw inertia helped the robot get further but did not keep the line. Iteration 4 versus iteration 1 showed that narrowing wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m gave a small slalom gain without hurting the oval, so turn authority is the lever still moving the slalom. I follow the Builder's intent and change only wheel_track, from 0.10 to 0.09 m. That adds about 11 percent more turn per unit of PWM difference. I keep the mass, body, span, lead, footprints, kp 3.6, kd 0.9, ki 0, base_speed 1.6 and last_direction unchanged, so the race isolates the drivetrain change. The oval has about 1.2 s of time margin, so it should absorb the change. The main risk is s-bend jitter from the higher effective turn gain, so steering_oscillation is measured on all three tracks. Expected: slalom line_loss_events near or below 1.0, max_error nearer 0.06, and the oval holding 20/20. No outcome is claimed for this package.
